title: Learning piano and brief lessons
summary: Toussaint cannot remember when he began piano, had only a couple of months of lessons, and the talk turns to old-timers' attitudes to reading music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: How were you when you started studying piano, shall we say?

I really don't know. It was somewhere down there before I recognized the world. By the time I recognized other things, I already knew to be in the family way. So, I don't know, give or take five, seven.
And did you have any lessons at all?
A little later on, I had a few, a couple of months. Not a few. Which didn't work out too well. But that's about the extent of a couple of months.
A little train. Years ago, the musicians used to have a soft joke. They'd say, can you read Yabba not enough to hurt my plane?
That was the attitude of a lot of real old timers.

For years of time, I'd hear that as a joke. They'd tune up and say good enough for jazz. They weren't concerned with things like that. Years ago, it was a whole different attitude. And of course, I think, here music still lives on New Orleans very much. As many people who applied about here could do that. Did you take lessons through the school or through a private teacher? Xavier. Xavier.

Xavier at that time. We had a junior school together. For kindergarten up. So that's where I attended. There was a 10-billton in the back. Even before that, the third floor of the front was called the 10-billton. So it was two months total there.
